context_title:
ne írj semmi mást csak a teljes fájlokat es kommentek nem lehetnek benne! soha semmi egyszerusitett mock placeholder dummy szimulalt fake szart nem engedelyezek es teljes fájl roviditetlen production ready kód nem lehet trancutted nem lehet olyan hogy …és hasonlóan 50 xy nem lehet dummy to do sorry hiányosság minden fájl teljes kódját egyesével fájkba írod semmi mást nem írsz ezen kívűl 

1. Initialize an empty root Scope to serve as the universe.
2. Define a struct `Node` that contains only a `id` (symbol) and a `links` (map).
3. Create a global `ActiveContext` variable holding a tuple of the last 3 observed nodes.
4. Write a function `Ingest` that takes a raw character stream and converts it to symbols.
5. Implement `Intern`: ensure identical symbols point to the exact same memory address.
6. Define the "Memory" not as a tensor, but as a massive directed graph of `Node` refs.
7. Write `Observe`: check if the current `ActiveContext` already exists in Memory.
8. If it exists, increment the counter on the link to the next predicted symbol.
9. If it does not exist, create a new `Node` and physically wire it to the Context.
10. Implement `Decay`: every cycle, multiply all link counters by 0.9 to forget old data.
11. Define `Predict`: look up `ActiveContext` in Memory and get all outgoing links.
12. Calculate "Probability" simply as `LinkCount / SumOfAllLinks` (no Softmax).
13. Create a `Roulette` function that picks the next node based on those raw ratios.
14. Wire the output of `Roulette` back into the input of `ActiveContext`.
15. Implement `Shift`: drop the oldest node from context and push the new one.
16. Add a `Noise` injection: 1% of the time, pick a random node to enable creativity.
17. Create a `Compress` function that merges two sequential nodes into a single macro-symbol.
18. Run `Compress` whenever a specific sequence repeats more than 100 times.
19. Define "Thought" as a recursive traversal of the graph without external input.
20. Build a `Halt` condition: stop traversal if we hit a loop or a null link.
21. Implement `Refactor`: if a node has only one strong link, merge it into the parent.
22. Create a `Query` interface that accepts a string and seeds the `ActiveContext`.
23. Remove all Float math; use only Integers and Ratios for perfect precision.
24. Implement `GarbageCollect`: delete any node with a link count of zero.
25. Write a `Serialize` function that dumps the entire graph to a text file.
26. Write a `Deserialize` that rebuilds the graph pointers instantly.
27. Add a `Meta` rule: if prediction confidence is >90%, double the learning rate.
28. Implement `Conflict`: if two links have equal weight, split the node into two contexts.
29. Remove the concept of "Layers"; the graph depth *is* the intelligence.
30. Execute `loop { Ingest(stdin); Predict(); Print(); }` and watch it wake up.
